solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stimulate pub, perhaps, by ever changing

parts.note: an inn is an example of a pub, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: something changing alters its form, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub is given a lift by constant changes of management or decor.
explanation.definitionFit: To innervate or innerve is to supply nervous energy to, so to rouse or invigorate.

clue.text: Ego upsetting one hard sergeant-major may get you this!

definitions.text: Ego upsetting one hard sergeant-major may get you this!
definitions.note: the whole clue: what an angry sergeant-major shouts

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the following letters upside down, so they read from the bottom

parts.note: Roman numeral one
H for hard, as on pencils
standard abbreviation for sergeant-major

explanation.surface: Annoying a tough sergeant-major with your self-importance will get you shouted at.
explanation.walkthrough: IMSHI is old army slang, from Arabic, for 'go away!' — just what an upset sergeant-major might bark at you.
explanation.definitionFit: Imshi is soldiers' slang for 'clear off', the dismissal a provoked sergeant-major would bellow.

clue.text: Service digger wanting third

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the third letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a navvy is a labourer who digs roads and canals

explanation.surface: A soldier or worker who can't count to three might be found in the services.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the third letter, a V, from NAVVY.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is one of the armed services, alongside the army and air force.

clue.text: Somehow get nearer outsider from Rouen?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unstated new arrangement

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A stranger from Normandy manages to approach more closely.
explanation.walkthrough: Rouen is a French city, so the outsider is named in French: étrangère, a female foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: In French étrangère is a foreign woman or stranger, an outsider as a native of Rouen would say.

clue.text: Take cap discarded from more posh parent

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top letter in a down entry, and it is thrown away

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions
posher things cost more, are dearer

explanation.surface: Remove your hat in front of a snootier mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the D from the top of DEARER and put R above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearer is someone who brings up young, which is what a parent does.

clue.text: Crabbit sort's preferable twa-handed drinker with no breadth

indicators.note: having no breadth means losing the letter that abbreviates breadth

parts.note: something preferable is better
in Scots a cap or caup is a wooden drinking bowl with two handles

explanation.surface: A Scottish grump insists a two-handled drinking vessel is better, minus a bit of width.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the B (breadth) from BETTER. Crabbit is Scots for bad-tempered, and twa is Scots for two.
explanation.definitionFit: An ettercap is Scots for a spider and, figuratively, a venomous, ill-tempered person.

clue.text: Pronoun for some informally here in US service

parts.note: in America 'yo!' is a reply meaning 'here!' at a roll call
use is service, as in 'of use'

explanation.surface: Someone notes an informal American pronoun used by people working in the US forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Youse is a dialect plural of you, the second-person pronoun for several people.

clue.text: Yes voter with term for Remain breed

parts.note: one voting yes is a yea

indicators.note: a term is an end, so only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Referendum talk: someone who voted yes alongside the end of the Remain camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Remain was the campaign to stay in the EU in Britain's 2016 referendum; here it just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To yean is to give birth to lambs or kids, an old verb for animals breeding.

clue.text: You're ideally stopping waste

definitions.note: loosely: a ureide is a compound derived from urea, a waste product

indicators.note: the answer is a stopper plugged inside the run of letters, sitting within those words

parts.note: letters running across the apostrophe and word break

explanation.surface: Ideally you'd stop wasting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a stretch: ureides are chemical derivatives of urea, the body's nitrogen waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A ureide is an organic compound formed from urea, which the body excretes as waste.

clue.text: Wallflower I caught in flipping harbour towns

indicators.note: these letters go inside the flipped word
flipping turns a word over so it reads the other way round

parts.note: harbour towns are ports
I is the Roman numeral one
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A shy person confesses to being trapped in some exasperating seaside towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallflower' suggests a shy partygoer, but it is literal: a plant growing on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a low succulent plant that commonly grows on old walls and rocks, so a flower of walls.

clue.text: Silver tree borders on lovely

parts.note: the elder is a tree

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A silver birch, perhaps, with lovely edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' looks like a metal or a birch; here it means silver-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver hair marks old age, so a silver generation is an elderly one.

clue.text: He favours flesh wobble, we hear, following excellent cut

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: MEAN is slang for excellent, as in 'a mean guitarist'; cut, it loses its last letter

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to teeter is to wobble

explanation.surface: A man who loves the flesh shakes after a fine haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the sound-alike after the cut-down word; 'flesh' means meat, not skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eater is someone who prefers animal flesh in their diet, a carnivore.

clue.text: Very good Latin for one who wasn't amused, an old monarch

parts.note: 'So!' can be an exclamation of approval, meaning very good or very well

parts.words: Latin for one who wasn't amused
parts.note: Victoria Regina, Latin for Queen Victoria, who supposedly said 'We are not amused'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fine Latin for Queen Victoria, the unamused one, is applied to a former ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: VR is the royal cipher of Victoria, from Victoria Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovran is Milton's spelling of sovereign, a reigning monarch.

clue.text: Fine deer coming back finding land given to servicemen?

parts.note: F for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, read backwards

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

explanation.surface: A splendid deer returns to discover its ancestral estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a feudal sense: land held in return for military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A feod, or feud, was a fief: land held from a lord in exchange for military service.

clue.text: Card containing area suited to scoring?

indicators.note: containing means holding something within, so the word wraps around a letter

parts.note: to scribble wool is to card it coarsely
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A scorecard has space that suits keeping scores in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a scorecard but is the verb for combing wool. The question mark flags scoring as writing marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Scribable means capable of being written or marked on, so fit to be scored.

clue.text: El Papa is one right into delegate in Rome finally

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following word

parts.note: an agent acts as a delegate
R for right
taken as written

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: The Pope is one who placed the right representative in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: El Papa is Spanish for the Pope; Pope Francis, from Buenos Aires, is an Argentine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope Francis was born in Argentina, so he is an example of an Argentine.

clue.text: Rest a steak transforming taste?

indicators.note: transforming changes the shape of the words before it into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
to taste food is, loosely, to eat it

explanation.surface: Letting a steak rest before serving improves its flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest a steak' reads as cooking advice; 'Rest' is the definition and the steak is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a seat is to sit down, which is to rest.

clue.text: I know beforehand I'm admired without judgement

definitions.note: the answer describing itself in the first person

parts.note: taken as written, placed beforehand
to con is an old verb meaning to know or learn

explanation.surface: A smug celebrity anticipates being adored uncritically.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a person revered uncritically, worshipped like a religious image.

clue.text: Airline attraction that is behind in Bannockburn

parts.note: BA is British Airways
a hook is a catchy attraction, as in a song's hook
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: An airline's lure, that is, a seat for your rear when flying to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Bannockburn is a Scottish battle site, flagging a Scots word; 'behind' means backside, not 'trailing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahookie is Scots slang for the buttocks, a person's behind.

clue.text: She lectures on fieldwork, mostly going west

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means running right to left, backwards
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a redan is a V-shaped fortification built in the field

explanation.surface: An academic lectures on practical research while travelling west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fieldwork' suggests research outside the lab, but it is a military earthwork. A Reader is a senior British university rank just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is a senior university lecturer, so someone whose job is to lecture.

clue.text: Fast track career from GP beginning with absolute kindness

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, Dr

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter only

parts.note: its first letter
grace is kindness or favour

explanation.surface: Someone leaves general practice for a fast-tracked career, beginning with total kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast track career' sounds like promotion; career here means a headlong rush down a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a sprint between cars down a straight track, a fast career in the sense of a dash.

clue.text: Ship to where Charon takes you? Forgotten land

definitions.note: 'Forgotten' flags that the word is obsolete

parts.note: Charon ferries the dead to Dis, the classical underworld
a bark or barque is a sailing ship

explanation.surface: A ship carries you to the underworld, a forgotten country.
explanation.walkthrough: The underworld piece is placed first although its clue words come second. 'Land' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Disbark is an obsolete word for disembark, to go ashore from a ship.

clue.text: Old slave women's anger during work

definitions.note: a dated phrase; slave is the verb

parts.note: W for women
ire is anger
in means during or at, as in 'in work'

explanation.surface: A former slave voices women's rage at their working conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slave' looks like a noun but is the verb, to toil.
explanation.definitionFit: To wire in is old slang for setting to work vigorously, to toil hard.

clue.text: Religious jurisdiction is cautious about what spell contains

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word wraps the other letters

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious

indicators.note: what a word contains is its inside, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: its inner letters

explanation.surface: A church authority is wary of what a magic spell might hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapelry is the district served by a chapel, an area of church jurisdiction.

clue.text: Thrust pawn, say, to capture rook

indicators.note: capturing holds something prisoner inside

parts.note: in chess a pawn is an example of a piece, hence 'say'
R is chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess move: push the pawn forward to take the rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrust' reads as advancing a pawn; it is the definition, a verb meaning stab.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to thrust a point through something, to stab or penetrate.

clue.text: Italian copper, antimony, and iridium run out

parts.note: Sb is the chemical symbol for antimony
Ir is the chemical symbol for iridium
ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: An Italian chemistry lesson: copper, antimony and iridium are used up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the third metal in the list but means a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sbirro is an Italian police officer, and copper is slang for a policeman.

clue.text: Para Handy's incandescent in the hold perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Scots for ablaze, aglow
second meaning: below, as on a ship's lower deck

explanation.walkthrough: Para Handy is the Scottish skipper of a cargo boat in Neil Munro's stories, signalling a Scots word; a hold is the cargo space below a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Alow means alight in Scots, and is also an old nautical word for below decks.

clue.text: Tips off before going into branch of the wartime Navy

indicators.note: going into means entering the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: the Women's Royal Naval Service, the Wrens
a is short for ante, Latin for before, as in a.m.

explanation.surface: Someone gives a warning before joining a naval unit in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn someone is to tip them off about a danger.

clue.text: Employee's final cutting fluke with my mere profile

indicators.note: cutting into a word slices it open to put something inside

parts.note: the fluke of an anchor or harpoon is its barb

indicators.note: final points to only the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: its last letter, ignoring the possessive
one's is the formal pronoun meaning my own

explanation.surface: A worker's last lucky break, together with my modest CV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluke' suggests luck but is the barbed point of a harpoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare bones of something are its essential outline, nothing more than a sketch.

clue.text: Fashion-eschewing itinerant trading odd bits

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions exchange places with each other

parts.note: a hobo is a wandering worker

explanation.surface: An unfashionable traveller dealing in odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first and third letters of HOBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Boho, short for bohemian, describes an unconventional style that ignores mainstream fashion.

clue.text: Roman emperor shortly back from Dobunni fighters

indicators.note: shortly means in abbreviated form, so the word is cut short

parts.note: imperator was the Roman title for emperor; shortened it is Imp.

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Roman-era warriors, recalled from an ancient British tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dobunni were an Iron Age tribe of the Cotswolds; only their final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.

clue.text: Grampa Simpson, among others, died laid up

parts.note: Grampa Simpson's name is Abe, one of many Abes
d. is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: The elderly Simpson grandfather and others died while confined to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abed means being in bed, as someone laid up with illness is.

clue.text: What tops espresso but a gold liquid which is thick?

indicators.note: but means except, so everything apart from that letter is kept

parts.note: crema is the golden foam on top of an espresso
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Is the golden crown on a coffee really a thick liquid?
explanation.definitionFit: Cremor is an old word for a thick juice or broth, a liquid with body.

clue.text: Firmly question murderer about quiet American nut

parts.note: in US slang to chin someone is to talk to them, to buttonhole them

indicators.note: about means around, so the word encloses the next letter

parts.note: Cain killed Abel, the first murderer
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: A detective grills a killer about a peculiar American nutcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' suggests a crazy person; it is a tree's fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinquapin or chincapin is a dwarf chestnut of North America, whose small edible nut bears the name.

clue.text: Japanese art's purpose? Slashing a winning blow

indicators.note: slashing cuts a word open, so the other word goes into the gap

parts.note: a KO, knockout, is a winning punch
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: What is a Japanese martial art for? Delivering a decisive cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slashing' fits the sword-fighting picture but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords.

clue.text: These are chunderous tourists one month off entering inch

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other word
off means removed, so a single abbreviation for month goes

parts.note: emmets, literally ants, is Cornish slang for tourists
in is the abbreviation for inch

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers being sick after a month of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: Chunder is Australian slang for vomit, so chunderous things make you throw up.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetins are alkaloids from ipecac root that induce vomiting.
